channel.title: Global Arbitration Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Arbitration Review (globalarbitrationreview.com)

item.title: UK court enforces US$66 billion Yukos awards
item.description: The Commercial Court in London has allowed the former majority shareholders of Yukos Oil Company to enforce Energy Charter Treaty awards worth more than US$66 billion against Russia, dismissing the state’s arguments that the awards were procured through fraud.

item.title: New faces on DIS council
item.description: The German Arbitation Institute, or DIS, has refreshed the membership of its arbitration council as Luther partner Richard Happ is re-elected as the council's president.

item.title: AIAC launches inaugural court
item.description: The Kuala Lumpur-based Asian International Arbitration Centre (AIAC) has revealed its inaugural court of arbitration, as several updates to Malaysia’s arbitration framework come into effect.

item.title: Chinese tech company defends ICC claim by Brazilian customer
item.description: A Chinese provider of digital payment solutions says it is defending an ICC claim potentially worth US$354 million brought by a Brazilian customer.

item.title: Shell fails to revive claim against LNG exporter
item.description: A New York state court has rejected Shell’s bid to revive its US$1.7 billion ICC claim against Venture Global over non-delivery of LNG cargoes – dismissing allegations that key documents were withheld during the arbitration as “pure speculation”.

item.title: Join us for GAR Academy Live: Advocacy Skills Workshop in Paris
item.description: Readers are invited to join us for the inaugural GAR Academy Live: Advocacy Skills Workshop, taking place during Paris Arbitration Week – where leading international arbitration practitioners will deliver an immersive, hands-on session on one of advocacy’s defining skills: cross-examination.

item.title: Freshfields lawyer goes solo in Rome
item.description: Lluís Paradell has left Freshfields after 27 years to launch an independent practice as counsel and arbitrator.

item.title: Ex-Argentine state lawyer joins Dechamps
item.description: Mariana Lozza, a former Argentine government lawyer who oversaw the state’s defence in several investment arbitrations, has joined UK-Argentine boutique Dechamps International Law as of counsel in Buenos Aires.

item.title: Pakistani oil block awards upheld in London
item.description: A UK judge has upheld a pair of ICC awards favouring a Canadian energy group in a dispute with its partner in two oil and gas blocks in Pakistan, rejecting arguments that Irish sole arbitrator Michael Collins SC exceeded his jurisdiction.

item.title: UK Supreme Court affirms no state immunity from ICSID awards
item.description: The UK’s Supreme Court has confirmed that Spain and Zimbabwe cannot invoke state immunity to oppose the enforcement of ICSID awards, saying that their accession to the ICSID Convention amounted to submission to the English courts’ jurisdiction.
